title: What to do next on jelly
ask: Log bugs as well when and if you find them or add evidence to existing
next: Log what is left outside Drop as issues, then start at the top of Do now

items.title: jelly ask says so when its --at matches nothing
items.reason: Small, and every agent that asks about a part of the page hits it.

items.title: jelly wait never misses a change made before it started listening
items.reason: #1 is built on it: an ask that waits must not miss a fast answer.

items.title: An agent can ask a question and get the answer in one command
items.reason: The loop agents use most: one command where there are two.

items.title: The first jelly see after the daemon starts returns a snapshot
items.reason: The cause is known now (F3), and the ask check already works round it the same way.

items.title: Only jelly's own pages and the CLI can talk to the daemon
items.reason: Found by reading code, never tried. Confirming it is small; it may turn out not to need a fix.

items.title: A shared jelly has no itemsAt, onAttention or asset
items.reason: A view that uses them throws in a shared file. A few lines in snapshot.js.

items.title: jelly is running whenever an agent reaches for it
items.reason: Removes the most common dead end, but you have a choice to make first: start at login only, or also on demand.

items.title: Every agent in a project sees everything the person did, even when several share it
items.reason: Only bites with two agents in one project, which has not happened yet.

items.title: jelly share drops images that state names
items.reason: Only assets the view names are inlined. Hit once, on the review recipe; screenshots were the way round.

items.title: Every command an agent reads prints one line per item, with --json for the rest
items.reason: Costs tokens and breaks nothing. Cheap enough that it could go first.

items.title: Headless Chrome lingers after it posts its snapshot
items.reason: The cause of #6, not a new bug: add it there as evidence.

items.title: jelly … | head panics on a broken pipe
items.reason: Rust's println does this when the reader closes early. Seen once, and only because I piped into head.
